literal: Prosperity and ruin by it because of arising, having guarded, ward off slip in speech.
translation: Since both prosperity and ruin arise from it, carefully guard against any slip in your speech.
modern: ஆக்கமும் அழிவும் ஒருவருடைய சொல்லாலேயே வருவதால், பேசும் சொல்லில் பிழை ஏற்படாமல் விழிப்புடன் காக்க வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes the profound impact of one's words. The words 'ākkam' (prosperity or constructive good) and 'kēṭu' (ruin or destructive evil) show that speech has the power to build up or tear down a person's life. Because such significant outcomes arise directly from speech, the speaker is advised to be extremely vigilant. The phrase 'kāttu ōmpal' (guard and protect) stresses the active, continuous effort required to prevent any 'cōrvu' (slip, error, or careless mistake) in what is said.
